title: Normalized finite tensor comparison respects its second input shift
statement: Fix a finite coefficient setting P [def-pur-conventions], 1 <= m <= P.level, an arbitrary scheme T, and derived fixed-scalar sheaves U,V over P.Coefficient. Let F be finiteTensorReduction and sigma its adjunction-induced finiteTensorScalarShift [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data], and put delta(U,V)=(finiteTensorCore.muIso U V).inv [def-pur-finite-signed-reduction-comparisons]. Write t1 and t2 for the native first- and second-variable derived tensor CommShift isomorphisms [def-weil-derived-tensor]. For every integer n, F(t2(U,V,n));sigma(n,U tensor V);delta(U,V)[n] = delta(U,V[n]);(1 tensor sigma(n,V));t2(FU,FV,n). Semicolons denote composition in application order. This assertion concerns only a shift of the second input; it does not assume a simultaneous tensor-shift compatibility.

proof.text: For the finite coefficient setting P, level 1 <= m <= P.level and arbitrary scheme T, use flat-term K-flat representatives of both derived inputs. Apply change of rings termwise. The changed complexes remain flat-term K-flat, without assuming the coefficient quotient flat. The localization equivalence permits the following natural comparisons to descend.

The second-input shift has factor (-1)^(np) on a summand whose first degree is p. Both routes preserve p and n, and coefficient extension carries -1 to -1. The cochain pullback tensor-shift theorem, applied to identity inverse image and the coefficient map, proves precisely this equality of cochain maps for all integers n. Equality is tested on every direct-sum summand, so no boundedness hypothesis is needed.

The counit-normalized scalar shift descends the degreewise identity on scalar extension. Its uniqueness identifies it with the shift transported by the exact restriction adjunction used in finiteTensorScalarShift: the adjunction unit/counit equations give the same representative square. Integer iteration and inverses give this identification at every n. The derived tensor shift descent identifies each tensor shift with the native fixed tensor CommShift instance, since both have the recorded cochain normalization. The unique normalized core identifies its inverse tensorator with the descended scalar-first binary map. Localize the cochain square and conjugate by the representative isomorphisms. Naturality and essential surjectivity give the displayed one-variable square for all U and V.

theorem finiteTensorShiftSecond (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) (m : ℕ) (hm : 1 ≤ m)
    (hmn : m ≤ P.level) (T : Scheme.{u})
    (U V : _root_.DerivedCategory
      (Sheaf (ProEt.topology T) (ModuleCat.{u + 1} P.Coefficient))) (n : ℤ) :
    (P.finiteTensorReduction m hm hmn T).map
        ((((curriedTensor _).obj U).commShiftIso n).hom.app V) ≫
      (P.finiteTensorScalarShift m hm hmn T n).hom.app (U ⊗ V) ≫
      ((P.finiteTensorCore m hm hmn T).μIso U V).inv⟦n⟧' =
    ((P.finiteTensorCore m hm hmn T).μIso U (V⟦n⟧)).inv ≫
      (P.finiteTensorReduction m hm hmn T).obj U ◁
        ((P.finiteTensorScalarShift m hm hmn T n).hom.app V) ≫
      ((((curriedTensor _).obj ((P.finiteTensorReduction m hm hmn T).obj U)).commShiftIso n).hom.app
        ((P.finiteTensorReduction m hm hmn T).obj V))
